chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what He made permissible for them therein.
Indeed, Satan is to man a clear enemy.
And He said (Exalted is He): They have no authority over them except those whom they delude themselves into thinking [Satan has authority over].

key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّهُمْ: He made permissible for them / He granted them license
key_terms.خَيَّلَتْ لَهُمْ أَنفُسُهُمْ: Their souls deluded them / made it appear to them

ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believing Muslims according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) clarification that Satan’s authority (hukm) over humans is not inherent but contingent upon their voluntary submission, distinguishing between those who are fully deluded and those who merely allow his influence. This narration underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (ikhtiyar), asserting that divine decree does not negate human responsibility for accepting or rejecting Satan's whispers. The explanation serves to comfort believers by affirming that spiritual bondage is a choice, thereby reinforcing the efficacy of conscious devotion and remembrance (dhikr) in breaking Satan's hold.
